original_record.question:
A rectangular piece of paper $A B C D$ with the measurements $4 \mathrm{~cm} \times 16 \mathrm{~cm}$ is folded along the line $\mathrm{MN}$ so that point $C$ coincides with point $A$ as shown. How big is the area of the quadrilateral ANMD'?
<image1>
original_record.subject: transformation geometry

inventory: One rectangle ABCD with dashed original right/top-right/bottom-right edges; fold MN; solid AB,BN,AM,AN and triangular folded boundary A–D′–M–N. Grey quadrilateral ANMD′. Curved arrow D toward D′. Labels A B C D M N D′.
audit.explicit_conditions: Question transformation and pictured connectivity, options, hole types/positions; no inferred metric labels.

answer_review.reason: Use A=(0,4), B=(0,0), C=(16,0), D=(16,4). Bisector fold 16x−4y=120 gives N=(7.5,0), M=(8.5,4), reflected D′=(32/17,128/17). Shoelace area ANMD′=32 cm², option C.
